Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Dry, itchy, red skin on hands and arms for several days, started after swimming; significant work-related stress; no prior skin disease.
- Relevant family medical history:  Father has asthma; mother has hayfever; no family history of skin problems.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Microgynon (contraceptive pill; dose/route/frequency not documented); uses coconut butter topically for skin.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Reports feeling very stressed due to work; feels tired; no mention of depression or self-harm.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.

- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings:  26-year-old woman with acute onset of dry, itchy, red skin on hands and arms, beginning after swimming; no previous personal or family history of skin disease; family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever); no systemic or infectious symptoms; denies alcohol/tobacco/drug use; feeling stressed and tired due to work.
- Differential diagnoses (from DDx and consistent with transcript):
    - Irritant contact dermatitis (High likelihood): Sudden onset after exposure to pool (chlorine likely), distribution on exposed skin, no prior skin disease—classic for irritant contact dermatitis.
    - Allergic contact dermatitis (Moderate likelihood): Possible sensitization to pool chemicals or other new contactant; less likely given absence of prior allergic reactions and localized distribution.
    - Xerosis due to dry weather (Low likelihood): Patient wondered if weather was a factor, but timeline supports irritant exposure.
- Working diagnosis:  Irritant contact dermatitis (most likely); monitor for progression or failure to improve.

Management Plan

- Recommended topical steroid cream to reduce inflammation (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advised use of emollients (moisturizers) regularly to alleviate dryness.
- Advised trial of over-the-counter oral antihistamines (e.g., Piriton, Loratadine) for itching.
- Provided patient information about dermatitis.
- Paracetamol and other painkillers not recommended as not indicated.
- Advised to return for in-person review if no improvement in a few days.
- No laboratory or further investigations indicated at present.
- Addressed work-related stress and validated concerns.
- No acute safety concerns identified.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood  
   - Justification: Sudden onset after swimming (chlorine exposure), affects only exposed skin, no prior history of similar symptoms, timeline and distribution classic for irritant dermatitis.
2. Allergic contact dermatitis – Moderate likelihood  
   - Justification: Possible reaction to new environmental contact (pool chemicals); family history of atopy may predispose, but less likely due to no prior personal atopic history, no other allergies.
3. Xerosis due to dry weather – Low likelihood  
   - Justification: Patient suspicion and current dry skin, but acute post-swimming onset and focal distribution less typical.

- Contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.
